title: Ruling: 'Rye beats Bari' in regular Arena
body: The Rye one-carry deck beats Bari–Oven at similar power only while Bari is at 8★ or less; at 8–10★ Bari and Oven, or with a clear spec lead, Bari–Oven wins. Many of the gallery's 'Rye beats Bari' screenshots are Rumble fights (server tags, +125/+175 medals, anonymous challengers), where the +30% DR buff lets Rye's tanks survive the dive; the same Rye deck that holds up to +6M in Rumble dies in 0.5 s to the same archetype in regular Arena. The regular-Arena evidence for the edge is thinner: one Season 5 win at 13.27M over a 20.4M server #2, a server that wiped its 5★ Bari decks with Rye, and a server #1 with an 8★ Bari who switched to Rye.

title: Ruling: Bari's star threshold against the Rye heal-tank decks
body: 5★ is a floor, not a win condition. Below 5★ Soul Guidance covers one charger and Bari decks lose to Rye heal-tank decks and to Crepe decks. From 5★ it covers two chargers (Oven and Cherry Cola), and posters call Bari the performance pick in regular Arena, yet same-power Rye decks still shred 5★ and 8★ Bari decks, and a 7★ Bari with an 8–9★ Oven is 'meh' at the top. At equal spec a Rye deck with an 8★ Rye beats a half-built 5★ Bari deck. At 8★+ Bari punches through Moon Rabbit, and at 10★ posters say the Rye deck can't hold at all. The deciding factors named alongside stars are gear and a merc Lv.4 captain.

title: Chargers dive the highest-ATK enemy
body: Oven Wanderer, Cherry Cola and Princess Bari dash at the highest-ATK enemy, as does Vampire's bat. That is almost always the enemy Milk, whose ATK is inflated and whose max HP is cut 20% by Passion Pay. Whoever loses their Milk or their Bari first loses the fight.

title: Princess Bari's Soul Guidance
body: Bari wraps herself and one random charge-type ally (two from 5★) in DMG reduction, lift and push immunity and periodic area damage. The EN skill panel at 8★ shows a 5.5 s cooldown, 32% DR and guiding damage of 127.8% of the guided cookie's ATK, which fits the leak that the aura damage scales on the wrapped cookie's ATK; a rough datamine puts DR at 40% at 9★. Push and lift immunity is why Crepe and Espresso displacement fails against chargers.

title: Moon Rabbit's debuff
body: Moon Rabbit lowers ATK and crit rate of enemies near her (about −50% ATK and −130% crit at 9★ per a rough datamine, radius about 4.2), so mostly the enemy front line and often their Milk, which shrinks Milk's team buff. Knocking her back before she transforms avoids the debuff. Players disagree whether she is mandatory insurance against Oven or wasted outside Bari decks.

title: The first cast wins
body: Whoever casts first nearly always wins, so Skill Haste decides fights: a CC landing on a cookie as its cooldown ends delays the cast, and a skill interrupted by CC still counts as cast. Against the Bari dive, the opening is survived by Ion's and Rockstar's shields after their Skill Ready buff, Doughnut's polymorph and Herb healing Milk. Rockstar's cycle is about 5 s including Skill Ready against Grapevine's 5.5 s.

title: ATK order routes the buffs
body: Pomegranate's Skill AMP beam (빨대) and Macaron's crit buff pick allies by ATK rank. Players steer them with ATK% runes and by levelling supports down: Milk first (for Passion Pay), then the carry. Milk's rank counts pet, perk and captain ATK% too. Skill AMP scales every buff and debuff, not only damage.

title: Formation geometry
body: The formation screen shows two rows of six. Left to right runs back line to front line: Macaron (range 7) and Oven sit in column 1 and Herb (range 1.25) and Moon Rabbit (range 1) in column 6, and the Herb at the top-right is the one that 'dies first'. An opponent's defense card appears to show the grid mirrored. Hound's Range synergy lines up Macaron's march; Milky Way breaks it.

title: Decoys and targeting
body: Rye's first volley fires where she faces; an isolated Schwarzwälder absorbed it and the Rye deck lost 3 of 3. A claim that Doughnut's polymorph targets the highest-HP enemy and Wind Archer's ultimate the nearest, so a tanky Oven soaks both, is unconfirmed.

title: Evasion against accuracy
body: Typical Arena evasion is about 650 and arena presets carry no accuracy, so a team built to about 1000 evasion makes attackers miss regardless of power. Switching to a stage preset with accuracy beats it. Opponent gear isn't visible before a fight, but names are, so evasion defenders get remembered.

title: Merc Lv.4 perks decide mirrors
body: A merc squad Lv.4 captain unlocks the second perk slot: Armor Repair (+10% DR with 3+ tanks) with Passion Pay. In the Rye mirror the side without perks set loses, and a Lv.3 squad is at a real disadvantage. Armor Repair needs three tank-type cookies (Hound, Ion and Moon Rabbit are all tanks); whether it counts them in-game is assumed, not verified.

title: Healing reduction ended the heal meta
body: Since Pinot Noir (8/27), her healing reduction beats heal-heavy decks even at a power deficit, and two healers suffice. Milk can't heal herself, so Herb stays; Ion's and Rockstar's shields aren't cut by it.

title: Displayed power overstates PvP strength
body: Power counts breakthrough, Stellar Link and lab research that PvP ignores, and arena presets show lower power because Skill Haste and crit RES add little to it (뻥투력). Power gaps of 2× are beaten routinely by matchup and gear.

title: Ruling: one 12-cookie team, not 'turtle vs charge'
body: The Rumble top 100 run one team. The DC lane read the board as 8–9-cookie support 'turtle' defenses plus a separate Oven + Bari charge deck, but the game hides some defenders (264 of 1,200 slots on 2026-09-27 14:33Z). Every fully revealed team carries Macaron, Pinot, Cheesecake, Pomegranate, Milk, Ion and Moon Rabbit, almost all of them also Oven and Bari; where Oven and Bari both show, at least four support-core cookies show too; and the #1's revealed count went from 8 to 12 within five hours. The turtle and the charge deck are partial views of the standard 12. The open caveat: empty slots are legal (a day-1 #3 fielded 9 cookies and 3 empty slots), so a few real 8–9-cookie defenses can't be ruled out.

title: Ruling: where 'Rye beats Bari' holds
body: In Rumble the Rye anti-charge deck beats Bari charge decks at mid-to-upper spec and similar power, because the +30% DR lets its tanks and healers survive the dive. At whale top-end (SR cookies at 10★) the buffed divers kill on contact, and no top-10 player runs a Rye defense: Rye is on 6 of the top 100, all ranked 30–100. One poster measured about 4 wins in 10 against 5★ Bari decks. Most gallery screenshots of Rye beating Bari are from this mode, not regular Arena.

title: What the Season 1 buff does to matchups
body: +30% max HP on Charge cookies is why Oven Wanderer went from unused to meta and why Bari decks work at 2–3★ here. +30% DR for all cookies and summons blunts burst: pure dive decks (Cool Mint + Cherry Cola + Oven + Bari) failed under it, the same Rye deck survives Bari–Oven here and dies in regular Arena, and Wizard decks that survive 10 s win. Commenters expect Oven and Bari to fall off when the buff rotates.

title: Princess Bari's Soul Guidance
body: Bari wraps herself and one random charge-type ally (two from 5★) in DR, lift and push immunity and area damage scaled on the wrapped cookie's ATK (127.8% at 8★ in the EN skill panel). In Rumble the Charge HP buff stacks with it, which is why a 1★ Bari still tops damage charts (1.58M).

title: Bari's stars in Rumble
body: Bari decks win here at 2★ and 3★ (Bari dealing 2.03M at 2★). The common advice is Oven 7★ and Bari 5★, from which Soul Guidance covers both Oven and Cherry Cola; the #3 player ran Bari 6★ with Moon Rabbit 7★. Below 5★, run one extra charger. A guide notes that a sub-5★ Bari is more viable in Rumble than in regular Arena because of the Charge HP buff.

title: ATK order routes the buffs
body: Pomegranate's beam and Macaron's crit buff go by ATK rank. Rye decks set Milk › Rye ≥ Pomegranate with ATK% on Rye and Macaron; one player holds Pinot at Lv.99 so the beam goes to Macaron. To route the beam onto Bari instead of Cherry Cola you strip Cherry Cola's ATK; at 5★ posters give up on it.

title: Moon Rabbit and Ion hold the dive
body: Moon Rabbit's ATK-down on the enemy Milk collapses their buff chain, and with Ion in front forms the wall charge decks couldn't break even at +2M. Divers such as Ion or Schwarzwälder can block Moon Rabbit before she reaches the back line.

title: Chargers with haste run in alone
body: Charge cookies run in from their slot; with Skill Haste or speed they engage before Milk's and Pomegranate's buffs land, which is why Oven gets defensive runes and no haste here.

title: Formation geometry
body: crumb.gg draws each defense as 12 slots in a 6-column by 2-row grid, and cookies hold stable slots (Macaron slot 0, Pomegranate 4, Moon Rabbit 11). Column 1 holds the longest-range cookies and column 6 the shortest, so left to right is back to front; the in-game formation screen shows the same layout. This is inferred from ranges; neither the site nor the game labels it.

title: Power doesn't decide rank
body: On the 2026-09-27 board the top-20 player with the most power (31.19e9) sits at #13 and the one with the least (14.20e9) at #16. Forum reports of 2× power upsets are common, explained by the gear preset, the Charge buff and matchup.

title: Matchmaking follows your points
body: Opponents are offered near your own points. Some players leave a 1-cookie defense to drop points and get easy targets and revenge fights; others keep a real defense because tickets are scarce and defense wins pay the medals.

title: Evasion is a wildcard
body: An 8.41M evasion deck beat 16.5M, and a charge deck on about 1,350 evasion takes no damage at equal power. Typical accuracy is about 1,000–1,050, and one claim puts the useful margin at about +400 over accuracy. Names are hidden in Rumble, so opponents can't remember who runs evasion; top rankers reportedly attack on their stage (accuracy) preset, possibly for this reason.
